title: Enriched transformations induce coherent nerve transformations
statement:
Use coherent transformations and internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the simplicial category of Kan complexes and its mapping complexes from [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Use small simplicial categories and the homotopy coherent nerve of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. A simplicial functor acts on objects and mapping simplicial sets and preserves composition and identity vertices. An enriched natural transformation consists of component vertices satisfying the naturality equality on every mapping simplicial set. The interval $[1]$ has objects $0,1$, one vertex in each mapping set except the empty mapping set from $1$ to $0$, and the forced compositions.

Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$. Let $C$ be a $\mathcal U'$-small simplicial category, let $T_0,T_1:C\to\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ be simplicial functors, and let $\tau:T_0\Rightarrow T_1$ be an enriched natural transformation whose naturality equation is an equality on each mapping simplicial set.  There is a simplicial functor $C\times[1]\to\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$ restricting to $T_0$ and $T_1$ at the endpoints and using $\tau$ on the cross mapping complexes.  Consequently its homotopy coherent nerve gives a coherent transformation
\[
N_{\mathrm{hc}}T_0\Rightarrow N_{\mathrm{hc}}T_1.
\]
This construction is natural under products, opposites, restriction, and whiskering, and the component at each object $c$ is the vertex $\tau_c$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(T_0c,T_1c)$. The compatibility with opposites is understood with its variance: for a simplicial target $B$, taking opposites gives the interval construction for $T_1^{\mathrm{op}}\Rightarrow T_0^{\mathrm{op}}:C^{\mathrm{op}}\to B^{\mathrm{op}}$, under $[1]^{\mathrm{op}}\cong[1]$ exchanging its endpoints. Here $B=\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$; no identification of $B^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $B$ is intended. Products mean the coordinatewise construction for product targets, and its postcomposition with any given enriched product functor; whiskering means precomposition or postcomposition by simplicial functors. The coherent transformation is an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(N_{\mathrm{hc}}C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$, so no local Kan hypothesis on $C$ is required.

source.place: Explicit enriched interval construction for an enriched natural transformation, with the coherent nerve of HTT Section 1.1.5 and Theorem 2.2.5.1; not a verbatim theorem of HTT.

proof.text:
Write $B=\operatorname{Kan}_{\mathcal U}$. Define $H(c,i)=T_i(c)$. On a same-endpoint mapping set use $T_i:C(c,d)\to B(T_i c,T_i d)$. On the cross mapping set from $(c,0)$ to $(d,1)$ use
$$H_{01}(f)=\tau_d\circ T_0(f)=T_1(f)\circ\tau_c.$$
The equality is exactly the assumed enriched naturality equality of simplicial maps, not just equality on vertices. Composition with a fixed vertex means composition after the constant simplicial map from the terminal simplicial set, hence is itself a simplicial map. On a mapping set from level $1$ to level $0$ there is the unique map out of the empty simplicial set. This defines all the mapping maps of $C\times[1]$.

proof.text:
Check the enriched functor axioms degreewise. For composable $m$-simplices $f:c\to d$ and $g:d\to e$, all at level $i$, the equation is the functor equation of $T_i$. For levels $0,0,1$ one has
$$H(g)H(f)=\tau_e T_0(g)T_0(f)=\tau_e T_0(gf)=H(gf).$$
For levels $0,1,1$ one has
$$H(g)H(f)=T_1(g)\tau_d T_0(f)=\tau_e T_0(g)T_0(f)=H(gf),$$
using enriched naturality for $g$ in degree $m$. These exhaust the nondecreasing triples of levels; for any other triple the domain mapping product is empty. Identities occur within one level, so are preserved by $T_i$. Thus $H$ is a simplicial functor with the required endpoint restrictions. These calculations work for any simplicial target $B$ and use no Kan filling or model structure.

proof.text:
For each $n$, abbreviate $Q_n=\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$, with the subset-poset mapping sets specified in the coherent-nerve statement. A functor $Q_n\to C\times[1]$ is exactly a pair of enriched functors to $C$ and to $[1]$: project all its object and mapping maps, and recover it by pairing. These inverse operations commute with restriction along every monotone map. Thus the degreewise bijections are a simplicial isomorphism
$$N_{\mathrm{hc}}(C\times[1])\cong N_{\mathrm{hc}}C\times N_{\mathrm{hc}}[1].$$
The cited statement identifies the coherent nerve of an ordinary discrete-enriched category with its ordinary nerve. A functor $[n]\to[1]$ is a weakly increasing map $[n]\to[1]$, so $N_{\mathrm{hc}}[1]=\Delta^1$, including its operators. Postcomposition with $H$ therefore defines a simplicial map $h:N_{\mathrm{hc}}C\times\Delta^1\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}B$.

proof.text: The space-category definition identifies $N_{\mathrm{hc}}B=\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$. The internal functor simplicial set has $1$-simplices precisely the maps $N_{\mathrm{hc}}C\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$, so $h$ is the claimed coherent transformation. Restriction at interval endpoint $i$ gives $N_{\mathrm{hc}}T_i$, because $H|_{C\times\{i\}}=T_i$. At $c$, restrict to the constant object functor at $c$ in the first coordinate. The edge is the enriched functor $Q_1\to B$ with objects $T_0c,T_1c$ and its unique nonidentity mapping vertex $H_{01}(1_c)=\tau_c$. This proves the asserted component identification directly, without passing to homotopy classes.

source.place: Adjunction calculation for K in D^b_c(X,R); agent-written enriched nerve support, explicit calculation step 4 (not a verbatim blueprint claim).

proof.text: For a simplicial functor $u:D\to C$, the cross mapping map of $H\circ(u\times\mathrm{id})$ is $\tau_{ud}T_0(u(f))$, exactly the formula for the restricted transformation. For a simplicial functor $v:B\to B'$, its postcomposition has cross map $v(\tau_d)v(T_0(f))$, exactly the formula for $v\tau$. Their endpoint formulas agree as well, so these are equal enriched functors. On every nerve simplex the construction is postcomposition of the representing enriched functor, which commutes with both equalities. This proves restriction and both kinds of whiskering, with all simplicial operators.

source.place: Adjunction calculation for K in D^b_c(X,R); agent-written enriched nerve support, explicit calculation step 5 (not a verbatim blueprint claim).

proof.text:
For a second transformation $\sigma:S_0\Rightarrow S_1$ on $D$ with simplicial target $B'$, form the external product on $C\times D$ with target $B\times B'$. Its interval functor is
$$(c,d,i)\longmapsto(H_\tau(c,i),H_\sigma(d,i)).$$
Its cross map on $(f,g)$ is $(\tau_{c'}T_0(f),\sigma_{d'}S_0(g))$, the cross formula for the product transformation. Thus it equals $(H_\tau\times H_\sigma)$ after the diagonal of the interval. Degreewise pairing of representing enriched functors, as in step 3, identifies its nerve with the paired coherent transformations on the same $\Delta^1$. Postcomposition with any specified simplicial functor $B\times B'\to E$ commutes by step 5. This includes objectwise products of space-valued functors via the enriched Cartesian product functor; its mapping maps send a pair of parameterized maps to their Cartesian product at the same parameter, so preserve identities and composition pointwise.

source.place: Adjunction calculation for K in D^b_c(X,R); agent-written enriched nerve support, explicit calculation step 6 (not a verbatim blueprint claim).

proof.text: For opposites use $B^{\mathrm{op}}(x,y)=B(y,x)$ with reversed composition. The functor $H^{\mathrm{op}}$ has source $C^{\mathrm{op}}\times[1]^{\mathrm{op}}$; exchanging interval endpoints makes it the interval construction for $T_1^{\mathrm{op}}\Rightarrow T_0^{\mathrm{op}}$. Indeed a cross map associated to $f\in C(d,c)$ is the opposite of $\tau_cT_0(f)=T_1(f)\tau_d$, precisely the cross formula in $B^{\mathrm{op}}$. To identify nerves explicitly, reverse $[n]$ by $r_n(i)=n-i$ and send a subset $S$ to $r_n(S)$. This gives an enriched isomorphism $Q_n^{\mathrm{op}}\cong Q_n$: it preserves inclusion of subsets, sends endpoints to reversed endpoints, and commutes with union. Consequently it identifies $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A^{\mathrm{op}})_n$ with $(N_{\mathrm{hc}}A)_n$ with reversed operators. For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, whose induced enriched functor sends a subset to its image as in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], those operators use $\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}(i)=n-\alpha(m-i)$; the identity $r_n\alpha=\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}r_m$ verifies their compatibility. Here the opposite of a simplicial set means exactly this reversal of operators. Applied to $H$, this identifies its opposite nerve map with the coherent transformation from $N_{\mathrm{hc}}T_1^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $N_{\mathrm{hc}}T_0^{\mathrm{op}}$ into $N_{\mathrm{hc}}B^{\mathrm{op}}$.
